comparator.name: Communicatie- en informatiewetenschappen
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 regulations require a 120 EC major and 60 EC of profiling. The major includes 60 EC of first-year foundations, 15 EC of other required courses, one 30 EC deepening package, 7.5 EC of thesis preparation and a 7.5 EC thesis. Media, Data and Society is the first of four packages listed in the regulations. The example preserves the open profiling choices.
components: Multimodale communicatie: analyse van tekst en beeld
Media, Data, Platform: communicatie in transformatie
Communiceren met infographics: ontwerp, cognitie en kritische analyse
Digital Methods & AI Literacy for Media and Communication Studies
Creator Cultures: Media Industries and the Digital Economy Cultures

routeSelection.basis: The target names the ordinary CIW bachelor but no deepening package. The adopted OER lists four equal-status compulsory-choice packages and places Media, data en maatschappij first. It is therefore selected neutrally from official order, not because of similarity to UCR; the 60-EC profiling space remains genuinely open.

core: Communication and media theory across language, image, audiovisual and digital forms
Meaning, rhetoric, persuasion, interaction and effective message design
Media technologies, platforms, institutions and their social, political and cultural contexts
Communication research, qualitative and quantitative methods, digital data and AI literacy
Professional and organisational communication, advice and improvement
Critical and ethical analysis of representation, identity, diversity and media power
adjacent: Cognition, emotion, psychology and audience response
Media industries, advertising, markets and creator economies
questions: How do messages, language and images influence people?
How do digital platforms and algorithms shape information and participation?
How can communication processes in organisations and society be analysed and improved?

candidates.label: Culture, communication and diversity
candidates.reason: Utrecht’s fourth package is a valid direction. UCR can study representation and identity through Media & Race, media narratives, social theory, rhetoric and diversity in organisations. The first three listed packages already supply three distinct options. Culture and diversity overlaps the selected options through those shared courses.

alternatives.label: Media, data and society
alternatives.labelReason: Media history and analysis, social theory, data analysis and AI ethics sustain the focus on media, data and society. Rhetoric, language and qualitative inquiry support communication study.
alternatives.concept: Study how media and digital platforms shape what people see and how they participate. Combine media history, representation and rhetoric with data analysis, machine learning and AI ethics to investigate those effects.
progression: Media and rhetorical foundations precede later media analysis and applied rhetoric. Introductory data handling precedes machine learning. The brain and behaviour gateway precedes psycholinguistics and advanced research methods.

alternatives.label: Media, communication and markets
alternatives.labelReason: Media history, representation and storytelling combine with audience research, economics, marketing and digital strategy. These support media and market study with an emphasis on organisations and consumers.
alternatives.concept: Study how media producers and organisations reach audiences. Combine media analysis with marketing, market research and digital strategy to investigate consumer decisions and how organisations respond.
progression: Rhetoric and media foundations precede advanced analysis and applied communication. Business and research gateways precede their dependent strategy, marketing, market research and leadership courses.
alternatives.distinctness: The markets option adds economics, marketing, consumer product design, digital strategy, market research and leadership. These support analysis of organisations and audiences. The media and data option gives more weight to algorithms, data, language and media’s social effects.

alternatives.label: Communication, organisation and interaction
alternatives.labelReason: Social psychology, rhetoric, leadership and negotiation provide sustained study of influence and interaction. Qualitative and quantitative methods support inquiry into communication within organisations.
alternatives.concept: Study how people make meaning, influence others and interact in organisations. Use social psychology and rhetoric to examine persuasion, then apply those ideas to leadership, negotiation and group decisions.
progression: Rhetoric and social psychology precede advanced influence and organisational study. The research gateway precedes dependent leadership and negotiation courses. Brain and behaviour precedes psycholinguistics and later psychology.
alternatives.distinctness: This option adds social psychology, experimental methods, negotiation, leadership and lifespan study. The media and data option centres media forms and computational methods, while the markets option centres consumer decisions and strategy.

blocks: Both introduce frameworks for analysing communication and its effects.
Both analyse meaning across text and audiovisual forms. UCR focuses on literary adaptation and film.
Both analyse language in interaction, including dialogue and pragmatic choices. Utrecht adds dedicated conversation analysis.
Both examine influence and the design of more effective messages.
Both examine AI’s effects and ethical implications. Utrecht focuses on how AI processes and generates language, while UCR studies a broader range of AI applications.
Both develop academic writing, argument and presentation. UCR also covers broader personal development.
Both introduce media institutions, forms and their relationship with society.
Both examine how media technologies develop and reshape communication, though UCR is more historically oriented.
Both consider media production, representation and participation on digital platforms. UCR situates those issues within American mainstream media.
Utrecht connects platform practices, datafication and social change. UCR treats related questions across media and social theory courses.
Both develop empirical research design, data collection, analysis and interpretation; UCR emphasises qualitative methodology.
Utrecht requires a proposal and research design for the thesis. UCR offers separate coursework in research design and systematic review.
Both teach ways to visualise information. UCR applies data visualisation across topics, while Utrecht also studies infographic design, cognition and interpretation.
Utrecht studies theories and politics of information. UCR covers data handling, media history and information systems across courses.
Both use computational analysis. UCR develops machine-learning methods, while Utrecht applies digital research and critical AI literacy to media and communication.
Utrecht requires an individual empirical research project and report. UCR offers optional independent research separately.
The comparator's 60-EC profiling space remains open, including its coherent 30-EC package requirement.

selection.assessment: The first three packages in Utrecht’s official order support distinct options in media and data, media and markets, and organisational interaction. The fourth package remains a valid direction, and courses on representation, identity and diversity contribute to the included options.

notes.text: Utrecht requires one coherent 30 EC package, CIW Lab and an individual thesis. The UCR options combine media and communication with data, markets or organisational interaction. Their research methods develop relevant skills, while Utrecht connects the lab directly to the thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht Communication and Information Studies examines how language, images and media shape what people understand and how they respond. Students learn communication research, complete a chosen package and carry out a supervised thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The three UCR options focus on media and data, audiences and markets, or communication in organisations. Utrecht combines these areas in a common core and offers four focused packages. This example shows its Media, Data and Society package.

curriculum.limitation: The example shows one of Utrecht’s four packages. The 60 EC of profiling remains available for choices within the degree rules.

componentNotes.ciw-lab: Complete the eight foundation courses and at least three of the four courses in the chosen package before entering CIW Lab.
componentNotes.ciw-thesis: The current route requires 120 EC before the thesis, including completion of CIW Lab and the foundation courses, and at least three courses from the chosen package. Two teachers assess the individual work.
componentNotes.ciw-profiling: Include a coherent 30 EC package, such as a minor, approved study abroad or a second CIW package. At least 15 of the 60 EC must be at level 2 or higher.
